content: Images uploaded to WikiDoc must be properly tagged to comply with copyright laws and to identify materials that are free for use. Since the servers are located in the United States, only U.S. copyright laws are applicable when national laws are relevant. For general rules on uploading images, refer to the WikiDoc Image Use Policy. Below are specific guidelines for tagging images: 1. Images should be tagged on their description pages using one of the provided tags to track their copyright status. For instructions on where to place these tags, refer to the Template Messages page. Tags should be placed on a separate line. 2. If an image is marked under a vague category, such as Copyrighted Free Use, you should specify the actual license or permission details somewhere in the description. 3. If an image requires attribution, clearly state who needs to be credited. Note that the GNU Free Documentation License (GFDL) mandates attribution. 4. If an image falls under multiple applicable categories, include all relevant tags. 5. Along with the tag, provide detailed information about the source or copyright holder of the image. 6. Pay attention to the file naming conventions for images to ensure clarity and organization. 7. Wikimedia Commons does not permit fair use materials, but such images can still be used on WikiDoc. Be aware that fair use is recognized in some countries but not in others. Certain images, including fair use ones, may need to be excluded from specific distributions, such as Mandriva Linux. 8. To assist with tagging untagged images, refer to the WikiDoc Untagged Images page. 9. Scroll down to view the complete set of tagging options available. For Image Creators: If you are the creator of an original work (e.g., photographer, designer), you do not need to review the entire list of tags. Ideally, you should license your work under a free license with minimal restrictions. These licenses are designed to maintain the freedom of your work rather than restrict its use. Some refer to this concept as copyleft. Each license is represented by a template, which displays a license box under your image. Copy the entire template, including the double braces, and paste it into the description when uploading your work. Alternatively, you can use the drop-down menu for tagging. {{GFDL-self}}: This tag applies to works licensed under the GNU Free Documentation License, originally created for free software documentation. {{CC-BY-SA}}: This Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike license allows free use, including commercial use, as long as you are credited as the creator. It also requires derivative works to use the same license. {{PD-self}}: This tag indicates that the work is in the public domain. However, there is some legal uncertainty about whether creators can release their work into the public domain. {{No rights reserved}}: This tag was developed to address the legal question of releasing works into the public domain. Refer to Wikipedia's guidelines on granting works into the public domain. Creators may license their works under multiple free licenses, and there is no limit to the number of license tags you can apply, though some may conflict with one another. Public Domain: Most images found on the internet are not in the public domain, even if no explicit copyright information is provided. Images qualify as public domain only if they meet specific criteria, such as being very old works, works by certain government employees, or works with an explicit written disclaimer of copyright by the author. For a chart on U.S. public domain regulations, refer to the provided link. Tags for Deprecated Images: Certain tags are used to mark images that are deprecated and will eventually be deleted. For example: {{PUIdisputed}}: Used for images with disputed copyright status. If unresolved, the image is typically deleted after 14 days. {{PUInonfree}}: Used for images with a noted non-free license. If no alternative license is found, these images are deleted after 14 days. Copyright Violations: Images that violate copyright laws are marked for quick deletion. For example: Template:Tlp: Used for images listed as copyright problems. Bad Images: Tags such as {{Missing image}} are used for images that cannot be deleted through standard procedures due to software bugs. These images must be manually deleted by a developer. Creating New Tags or Subcategories: If you are uploading a large collection of images, consider creating a new tag and subcategory for them. Before doing so, propose the tag on the relevant discussion page to avoid issues such as redundancy, vagueness, or licensing concerns. If you are unfamiliar with creating templates that add images to categories, seek assistance to avoid errors. Be sure to add the Category: Image copyright tags to the template. Image Template Notice: Each copyright tag, such as {{Fairuse}}, should correspond to a category. Adding such a tag to an image will automatically place it in the appropriate category, as the template should already belong to that category.
